summary: Establishes the agency's quantitative compliance monitoring program: KPI definitions, measurement methodology, monthly Compliance Dashboard, quarterly Compliance Summary, semi-annual Governing Body report, corrective action triggers (Green/Yellow/Red), and QAPI integration per 42 CFR 484.65.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Compliance KPI dashboard with monthly measurement records
Quarterly compliance summary reports with corrective action documentation
Semi-annual governing body compliance presentation records
QAPI-integrated compliance monitoring data with trend analysis
justification: Corridor rows 1-015 'Performance Improvement Program' and 1-016 'QAPI Program' (HH1-7A) implement 42 CFR §484.65, which requires a formal QAPI program including systematic quality monitoring. EN-CM-001 explicitly cites 42 CFR §484.65 and establishes QAPI integration as a requirement. PARTIAL because the QAPI rows establish the performance monitoring obligation, but EN-CM-001 extends this into an enterprise compliance metrics architecture — KPI definitions, dashboard infrastructure, traffic-light corrective action triggers, and governing body reporting cadence. These are modern compliance intelligence governance tools that exceed the Corridor's general QAPI program row. The QAPI integration component aligns directly; the enterprise metrics platform is a Modern Operational Governance Layer above the Corridor framework.

summary: Establishes governance rules for the complete policy lifecycle: creation, approval, active deployment, scheduled review (reaffirmation or revision), triggered review, sunset, and archival. Defines version numbering, overdue review escalation thresholds, and permanent version history retention.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs policy lifecycle management as a governance discipline. While ACHC and CoP require that clinical policies and procedures exist and be reviewed periodically (Corridor row 1-014 'Clinical Policies and Procedures' covers policy existence), the governance infrastructure for managing the policy lifecycle itself — creation workflows, approval chains, version numbering schema, overdue review escalation, sunset procedures, and permanent archival — is a platform governance function with no Corridor crosswalk equivalent. This policy governs the system that manages all other policies; it operates at a meta-governance layer entirely outside the Corridor's regulatory crosswalk.

summary: Establishes the master taxonomy structure for the agency's policy library: domain/subdomain/policy hierarchy, Policy ID naming schema, Tier classification standards (REQUIRED/ESSENTIAL/RECOMMENDED/GOOD TO HAVE), Policy Registry requirements, and regulatory cross-reference mapping.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs enterprise policy taxonomy and classification governance. The Corridor requires that clinical policies exist and be organized (1-014), but the taxonomy infrastructure governing how policies are classified, named, tiered, registered, and cross-referenced is a knowledge management and compliance ontology function with no regulatory crosswalk equivalent. This policy defines the classification system that the Corridor tagging exercise itself operates within — it is foundationally meta-governance, governing the governance of other policies. No accreditation framework governs this layer.

policyTitle: Policy Execution, Workflow Enforcement & Evidence Traceability
summary: Defines enterprise controls for policy execution workflows, control-point enforcement, and evidence traceability across modules.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs policy execution workflow infrastructure, control-point enforcement, or evidence traceability as a platform function. While surveyors validate that policies are implemented and evidence exists (the survey evidence methods cited throughout this tagging exercise), the system that enforces workflow execution, monitors control points, and maintains cross-module evidence traceability is a compliance platform engineering concept with no accreditation framework equivalent. This policy governs the enforcement and traceability machinery of the compliance system itself — a pure Modern Operational Governance Layer artifact that emerges from the architecture of the compliance platform rather than any regulatory requirement. It is the infrastructure that makes all other policy evidence surveyable, but is itself not anchored to any Corridor row.
